critic_text:
Hold. This is a different unit. The old audit does not cover it.

The defect is the same; the fix is not. The audited unit was: documented variable in the command, unrooted search everywhere else, no claim in undocumented layers, docs describe a layout they do not contract. The replacement is: probe an env var with `echo`, then Glob at `~/.claude/plugins`, uniformly, in all eight files. That withdraws the non-goal that forbade claiming the variable where the platform does not document it, and it withdraws “a mechanism, not a corrected path.” A parent directory that survived one move is still a guessed layout. I am not auditing a patched AC2; I am looking at a new design that has not been specified far enough to implement.

The binary check is the right kind of evidence and it cuts against the new primary. You showed `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}` is an env var for hook and MCP spawns, not a prose placeholder. That kills old AC2. It does not license `echo "$CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT"` from command, agent, or skill bash. Those are different spawn paths. You have not said you watched echo print a non-empty value in any of those layers in an install — which is the observation this whole effort exists to start making.

That hole is the original defect’s shape. If the var is not injected, echo is empty, the instruction says “use the Glob,” and the primary never fails in production. Empty-because-not-injected and empty-because-unset are indistinguishable, so the echo branch is unfalsifiable. Article 3 has nothing to watch fail. Do not put echo in the eight files until it is watched non-empty in that layer; until then the honest procedure is the Glob root alone.

`~/.claude/plugins` as that root is the one defensible new piece. It is the prefix of both the dead cache layout and the observed marketplaces layout, so it is a better Glob root than `cache/` and a better one than cwd. It is not layout-proof. Write it as an observed stable prefix, not as the mechanism that survives the next move.

“Uniform across all eight files” is a category error. INSTALL.md and `docs/plugin-authoring.md` do not resolve bundled files. They describe a layout. That is why AC4 exists and why the AC1 allowlist exists. Instructing those two to `echo` then Glob undoes both. Runtime files get a resolver; those two get the observed-layout description. That split is the unit.

AC1 still has a matcher hole, one level up. The runtime files must now contain `~/.claude/plugins` as a Glob root. The check forbids absolute/`~`-rooted paths naming a plugin install directory *below* that path, in any separator style, except the two docs and itself. Unless the spec says the parent is the allowed root and the checker distinguishes `~/.claude/plugins` from `~/.claude/plugins/cache` (and `marketplaces\`, `$HOME`, `%USERPROFILE%`), T4 will either fail the six runtime files or miss the literals it exists to catch.

“Use it if non-empty” is not a procedure. Old AC2 named the join (`…/agents/quorum-orchestrator.md`). The replacement does not say what to join, how to Glob under a successful echo, or which hit to take when `~/.claude/plugins/**/<file>` matches more than one plugin. AC1 will not catch a missing procedure; it only bans child literals. If echo-then-Glob is the new guarantee, it needs a named shape per file and an assertion that shape is present — or it is a description, and the only guarantee is the literal ban.

A coherent restatement of this new unit, small enough to implement: (1) six runtime files Glob rooted at `~/.claude/plugins`, no cache/marketplaces fallbacks; echo only if watched non-empty in that layer in an install; (2) two docs describe the observed layout as observed; (3) check.py forbids child install-path literals except those two docs and itself, and allows the parent as a Glob root; (4) name the join and the multiple-match rule. Until that is the spec, do not treat the previous audit as covering the work.

- severity: blocker — echo of CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT is prescribed in command/agent/skill layers the binary check does not support; empty echo is indistinguishable from “never injected,” so the primary is unfalsifiable and the silent fallback is the original defect
- severity: major — “uniform across all eight files” treats INSTALL.md and docs/plugin-authoring.md as resolvers; they are the AC4/allowlist docs, not runtime lookup
- severity: major — AC1 forbids paths below ~/.claude/plugins while the new Glob root is that path; the matcher still does not say how it distinguishes parent from child, so T4 can fail the runtime files or miss cache/
- severity: major — “use it if non-empty” names no join, no multiple-match rule, and no assertion the procedure is present; AC1 only bans child literals
verdict: concerns

Hold.

The echo-then-Glob **procedure** is statically assertable, but successful file resolution is not. A `check.py` assertion can verify that both branches and an explicit empty-result failure action are present; it cannot prove that prose can execute `echo`, receive its output, and pass that path to a file-reading tool in commands, agents, and skills.

Therefore either:

- demote successful resolution to a description, backed by a manual real-install smoke test; or
- retain it as a guarantee and add an `e2e.py` test that exercises each supported layer in a real installed plugin.

Also specify that `~/.claude/plugins` is an observed current search root, not a future-proof contract. The fallback survives the known cache-to-marketplaces change, but does not by itself survive the platform moving the plugin root.

- severity: major — Successful prose-level resolution is unverified; static checks cannot establish that the echo output reaches file lookup

verdict: concerns

## Direct answer: withdraw.

Echo-then-Glob removes the 5-of-8 hole, and the Glob branch's base is sound, not moved.

**Why the echo branch is legitimate now.** Your binary reading is the right evidence and the right conclusion: placeholder substitution for hook commands and MCP configs is not prose substitution, and an environment variable reaching a spawned shell is not a template being rewritten. The original AC2 conflated the two. The replacement design is immune to that conflation because it *tests* rather than asserts: `echo "$CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT"` is a runtime observation. Where the platform sets it for spawned shells (the documented command case), it works. Where it doesn't (agents, skills — unknown), the empty output routes to the Glob branch. Every layer gets a mechanism that verifies before it trusts, which is precisely the standard the layout row was held to. Uniformity is achieved without "probably works" — that resolves my second question from the first round rather than conceding it.

**Why the Glob base is not moved-rather-than-fixed.** My original base problem had three parts, and all three are addressed:

1. *Reachability* — the old "unrooted search" rooted implicitly at the agent's cwd, which cannot reach `~/.claude/...`. Rooting explicitly at `~/.claude/plugins` is an absolute path the agent can construct and Glob from. Fixed, not relocated.
2. *Stability of the anchor* — `~/.claude/plugins` is the deepest segment present in *both* observed layouts (the departed cache shape and the current marketplaces shape). It is the only base for which you have direct evidence of surviving exactly the change that bit you. Choosing anything deeper would re-introduce the bet that broke; choosing anything shallower gains nothing.
3. *Failure mode if the anchor ever moves* — the Glob finds nothing, and AC3's stated "finds nothing" recourse fires. That degrades to honest failure, not silent-wrong-file. A base you cannot prove stable is acceptable when its failure is loud; that was never true of the literal fallbacks.

So the residual dependence on `~/.claude/plugins` is real but correctly priced.

## Residual gaps — all small, all one-line fixes

- **Glob multi-match is unspecified.** AC3 requires each search to state what to do when it finds *nothing*; it must also state what to do when it finds *several* — the same plugin directory name from two marketplaces, or stale `<hash>` copies if the cache shape ever returns. Silently picking the first match recreates the original defect class (authoritative-looking, silently wrong), with the sole mitigation that the matches are at least visible to the agent. Add a disambiguation clause (prefer the path whose marketplace segment matches, else stop and report).
- **The echo branch trusts presence, not identity.** "If it is non-empty, the bundled file is beneath it" asserts. A non-empty-but-wrong root (e.g., a hook-spawned shell carrying another plugin's root) needs: check the target file exists beneath it; if absent, fall through to the Glob branch.
- **`~/.claude/plugins` should get the AC4 treatment.** It is now the load-bearing anchor of all eight files; the docs should mark it observed-stable-across-one-layout-change, not contracted — same epistemic label as the layout itself.
- **The allowlist grants blanket immunity to two files.** "Forbids install-path literals everywhere except two named documentation files" permits *any* literal in those files — including the cache-shaped one being expelled. Scope it: the observed-layout pattern is permitted only in the allowlisted files; the cache pattern is forbidden everywhere, docs included.
- **AC2's tracked text still mandates the disproven mechanism.** "Resolves its orchestrator agent with `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}`" now describes an instruction that would not work. Rewrite the criterion's text, not just its interpretation, or the gate will check the old words against the new work.
- **Shell portability.** `echo "$CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT"` assumes a POSIX shell; this spec once cared enough to ship Windows examples. State the bash assumption explicitly or give the portable form.

- severity: minor — Glob branch has no stated recourse for multiple matches (same plugin name across marketplaces, or stale hash dirs); AC3's "finds nothing" clause needs a "finds several" sibling or the silently-wrong-file class survives in miniature
- severity: minor — echo branch trusts any non-empty value; needs an existence check on the target file with fall-through to Glob, else a foreign plugin's root yields a confident wrong path
- severity: minor — ~/.claude/plugins is now the single anchor for all eight files but is not yet given the AC4 observed-not-contracted marking in the docs
- severity: minor — allowlist as described gives the two doc files blanket immunity, including against reintroduction of the cache-shaped literal being expelled; restrict the allowance to the observed-layout pattern
- severity: minor — AC2's text still requires ${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT} prose substitution, the mechanism just disproven; the criterion must be rewritten so the gate does not check stale words
- severity: minor — echo "$VAR" assumes bash; the spec previously shipped Windows examples, so state the shell assumption or use a portable form

verdict: pass
